title: Compositional throughput targets and lattice-based scaling engine
creator: Liam Morales
description:
Goal: design and implement a compositional autoscaling engine for Dedicated capacity that enforces tenant-level throughput guarantees while keeping fleet cost and stability within defined safety limits.

Problem summary: current autoscalers rely on single-metric thresholds (e.g., GPU util or queue length) and either oscillate or under-provision for tail latency-sensitive tenants. We need a single decision layer that combines multiple observable signals, supports target composition (throughput + latency + KV cache hit-rate), and applies conservative ramp/surge controls to avoid noisy scaling across heterogeneous pools.

Proposed approach: build a lattice-based scaler that computes a set of candidate scale actions from independent "scaling dimensions" and then reduces them deterministically into a single safe action. Scaling dimensions include:
- throughput demand (tokens/sec and requests/sec per-tenant) with short-window EWMA forecast
- p95 and p99 generation latency relative to tenant SLA
- queue depth and request age (headroom indicator)
- KV cache hit rate delta (indicates cold starts cost)
- GPU/CPU/%vram utilization and kernel stall signals

Each dimension produces a suggested delta (replicas or worker-shards) with an associated confidence and cost estimate. The lattice reduction applies configurable operators in this order: apply per-tenant priority modifiers, enforce global min/max fleet caps, clamp to concurrent ramp limits, then apply safety envelopes (minute-based step limits and hourly budget). Final action is annotated with reason and cost delta for observability.

Algorithms and controls:
- Forecasting: 5s evaluation cadence, EWMA with multiple half-lives plus AR(1) short-horizon predictor; fallback to raw short-window peak if signal is non-stationary.
- Scaling law: Combine additive-increase for cautious growth and multiplicative-decrease on cooldowns to quickly shed excess capacity when load drops.
- Hysteresis: dynamic hold-time tied to observed SLA breach severity (p95 breaches -> longer hold).
- Ramp limits: configurable global and pool-level ramp_rate (replicas/min) and per-tenant burst tokens consumed from a shared surge pool.
- Emergency mode: if sustained queue growth > X over Y seconds and p99 breaches, allow temporary pre-authorized surge up to emergency_cap (requires cost guardrail).

Safety limits:
- hard min/max replicas per pool, tenant-level minimum reservation, and global fleet headroom floor (percent of reserved GPUs to keep for preemption-free fallbacks).
- cooldowns and step ceilings prevent >50% capacity change within a 10-minute window unless emergency mode triggers.
- automatic rollback triggers if rollout causes >5% increase in error-rate or resource starvation within the canary cohort.

Observability & diagnostics: every decision emits: contributing signals, per-dimension suggestions, reduced action, estimated cost delta, and a compact justification string. Add new Grafana dashboards and alerting: scale-ops, predicted-vs-actual, and canary-regressions.

Testing and validation: run workload replay sims using production traffic traces (last 30 days) against multiple scaling policies. Benchmarks from simulation: target composition policy reduces SLA violations by ~30% vs baseline stepper at cost +18% in median tests; still need edge-case runs (tenant burst co-tenancy).

Implementation plan: phase 1 (core lattice reducer + signal adapters) -> phase 2 (ramp/surge pool and emergency mode) -> phase 3 (canary rollout + console controls). Phase 1 is scoped for this cycle.

Rollout: canary to Dedicated pool A with 10 low-risk tenants for 2 weeks, monitor key metrics (p95 latency, queue depth, scale-churn, cost delta). Provide kill-switch and feature flag to fall back to legacy autoscaler.

Open questions: specific per-tenant priority weight encoding, exact emergency_cap sizing (trade-off with committed capacity), integration surface with routing fallback policies.

Acceptance criteria: automated simulation pass with no regressions on SLA for 95% of tenant synthetic mixes, unit + e2e tests, console shows per-action justification, and canary run metrics meet safety gates.
